title: Emergent Symmetries in Ensemble Averages
abstract: It is widely believed that there are no exact global symmetries in quantum gravity. We review recent works showing that global symmetries can nevertheless emerge after ensemble averages of theories, as encountered in holography. As a precision case study, we discuss the ensemble average of two-dimensional Narain-type conformal field theories associated with an even quadratic form of general signature, which is computed by the Siegel-Weil formula and interpreted as a sum over geometries in a three-dimensional Abelian Chern-Simons theory. Global symmetries of the bulk anyons can emerge after the average, as T-dualities relating different theories in the ensemble are "folded" into symmetries of a single theory (duality origami). We discuss the relation to the Swampland program, including the emergence of global symmetries at infinite distance. Finally, we recast strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SWSSB) of mixed states as an emergence of symmetries in ensemble averages; in holography, wormholes connecting the two sides of a thermofield-double construction provide its bulk realization. This motivates a new Swampland conjecture.
summary: This paper explores the mechanism by which global symmetries can appear in quantum gravity theories when averaging over an ensemble of possibilities. It uses advanced mathematical tools, like the Siegel-Weil formula applied to CFTs, to show that this averaging process yields symmetries that are otherwise absent. This work proposes a new conjecture linking symmetry breaking in mixed states to the structure of ensemble averages in holography.
main_problem: The paper investigates how global symmetries, generally believed absent in quantum gravity, can emerge when considering ensemble averages of quantum field theories.
main_result: Global symmetries emerge from the ensemble average calculation, which is mathematically realized by equating the average partition function to a specific Eisenstein series, suggesting a mechanism for symmetry emergence in holographic contexts.
method: The core method involves computing ensemble averages of partition functions (theta functions) using the Siegel-Weil formula, relating them to sums over bulk geometries (Eisenstein series).
model_or_system: The study uses 2D Narain-type CFTs whose ensemble average is dual to a 3D Abelian Chern-Simons theory in the context of holography. It also analyzes Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SWSSB) in the thermofield-double construction.
key_observables: The ensemble average of the theta function $\langle \vartheta_{Q, \alpha} angle$, the R\'enyi-2 correlator, and the resulting Eisenstein series $E_{Q, \alpha}$.
important_parameters: The quadratic form $Q(\ell)$, the moduli space $M_Q$, and the large-distance limit $|x-y| 	o \infty$ for correlation functions.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the ensemble average resolves the 'factorization puzzle' in AdS/CFT, and it proposes a new Swampland conjecture based on these findings.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the 'factorization puzzle,' contrasting factorized contributions from disconnected bulk geometries versus non-factorizing contributions from wormhole geometries, which the ensemble average is expected to resolve.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the problem of symmetry emergence in quantum gravity, to applying the Siegel-Weil formula to CFT ensembles, and finally generalizing the concept to recast SWSSB in holographic models.
why_interesting: The concept of symmetry emergence via averaging is a powerful theoretical tool that connects concepts from condensed matter (topological order, symmetry breaking) to fundamental questions in quantum gravity and string theory.

figures.caption: Figure 1: The factorization puzzle [12, 13]. The two boundary CFTs live on (here genus-two) Riemann surfaces, drawn in white, and the shaded regions represent the bulk, whose boundaries are these surfaces. (a) Disconnected bulk geometries, each filling in one of the boundaries, reproduce the factorized answer ZCFT1 ·ZCFT2. (b) The gravitational path integral also includes wormhole geometries connecting the two boundaries, whose contributions do not factorize. The puzzle can be resolved if the bulk computes the ensemble average on the boundary, for which ⟨ZCFT,1⟩⟨ZCFT,2⟩̸= ⟨ZCFT,1 · ZCFT,2⟩.
